# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ - The middle of December was a depressing time for the precious metals markets, with all of the metals losing grounds in price terms as the Euro weakened. ETF holdings and futures positions declined for each metal as a falling price and the approaching year-end made it hard for even the most bullish investor to find the short term risk reward trade-off attractive. All four metals lost ground, with the first signs of timid bearishness reappearing in the gold market for some considerable period of time. • Net long speculative positions fell for each of the precious metals in the week to the 13th of December. For gold, this was simple long liquidation but for platinum, there was evidence of growing short tem bearish sentiment. Given the strength of the US Dollar and the decline in prices since that point, we expect further decreases in positioning to be revealed in the next Commitment of Traders Report. • ETF holdings fell for all four of the main precious metals in the week to the 16th of December. For palladium, platinum and silver, this was a continuation of the recent selling pressure. For gold, though, this marked the end of a period of ETF buying. Although risk aversion would tend to drive further buying, a sharp decrease in the price typically drives some of the most recent buyers of ETF metal out of the market. ##### **David Jollie** **david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **19 December 2011** ##### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 ##### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 ##### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 ##### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 ##### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **19 December 2011** ### **Gold CFTC data to 13 December 2011; ETF data to 16 December 2011.** #### **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

Gold made a determined attempt to reclaim the $1,750 level it had fallen through on the 5th but stalled at $1,746 on the 8th when news emerged that the ECB was not considering a wholesale purchase of European sovereign bonds. Gold selling emerged as the market sold off assets almost regardless of their fundamentals. Gold slumped to $1,706 by the end of the day and a negative trend was firmly established. The news that 26 of the 27 EU countries had agreed in principle to a fiscal compact did not impress the market as it failed to deal with today’s issues of solvency and liquidity. On the 12th, the market gave its verdict, driving the Euro downwards and gold down too. On the 13th, the gold price approached its 200 day moving average but did not bounce off this level, falling though instead, to a low of $1,568 on the 14th. While this hurt short term sentiment, it failed to generate outright bearishness and, with the Euro a little more stable, gold has once again targeted the $1,600 level. #### **Gold Exchange Investment, April 09—December 11** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

- Net long speculative gold positions on COMEX fell by 2.6 million ounces in the week to the 13th of December to a total of 20 million ounces. Long liquidation was the order of the day as a falling price drove some selling. There was, though, little evidence of investors taking additional short positions. However, since that date, a further decline in the gold price has driven bearish sentiment higher, suggesting that an increase in short positioning could be reported in the next Commitment of Traders Report. - Global Exchange Traded Fund holdings of gold fell by 364,000 ounces in the week to the 16th of December to a touch below 70 million ounces. This was the first week of net selling following nine weeks o

f net buying, in which time three million ounces of gold were purchased. Most of the European funds saw mild buying interest on risk aversion. - Silver’s price action was just as negative as gold’s in the second week of December 2011. Wide swings in the price have been commonplace this year but the move down from $32.80 on the 5th to its brief low of $28.15 or thereabouts on the 14th was still brutal, squeezing the optimism from the market. As with the other metals, the real driving forces were macroeconomic in nature with waning confidence in the Euro zone’s ability or desire to save itself the main drive for a weakening Euro and plunging precious metals prices. Silver’s attempts at recovery since the lows have been unconvincing as it failed to reach $30. In the short term, with demand weak and the year-end approaching, silver may struggle to gain ground. Looking into next year, risk-driven buying of gold could contribute some strength to the silver price. - Net long speculative positions in silver on COMEX fell again in the second week of December, decr

easing from 137.7 million ounces to 125.8 million ounces. In recent weeks, this level of speculative interest has seemed fairly solid, so it will be interesting to see whether the price fall at the end of last week has driven an increase in short interest. - There was net selling from the silver ETFs in the week to the 16th of December. 1.3 million ounces of metal were sold, the fifth week in the last six during which investors have redeemed more ETF shares than they created. Although this sounds bearish, flows have been relatively small and total holdings have changed little since the middle of 2011. 3 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **19 December 2011** ### **Platinum CFTC data to 13 December 2011; ETF data to 16 December 2011.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Platinum Investment (oz)** ||**Nymex**||||**TOCOM**|**Net total**|**Price**| |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| |||_Futures_

- The platinum price was weak from the 6th of December to the 19th. A weak Euro and a falling gold price set a bearish tone and platinum steadily slipped from a high of $1,537 on the 7th to successive lows of $1,490 on the 9th, $1,483 on the 12th and $1,469 early on the 14th. The final push of the foreign exchange markets to take the Euro below $1.30 applied the finishing touch, sending platinum to a very brief low of $1,380 on the 15th. In the longer term, prices this low cannot be sustained without supply destruction within the mining sector. However, investors were looking at the short term and

remain somewhat bearish at close to $1,415 an ounce. Encouragingly, there was one positive sign in that the spread between gold and platinum narrowed, moving in platinum’s favour. It has, however, widened somewhat since the 14th as metal prices have recovered. - Falling platinum prices drove further increases in short positioning for this metal on NYMEX in the week to the 13th of December. Although current price levels do not seem sustainable over the short term, an increasing number of investors bet on falling prices, demonstrating how much of the interest on NYMEX is short term in nature. Net long speculative NYMEX positions fell by 67,000 ounces during the week to 1.13 million ounces. - The week to the 16th of December saw renewed selling from the platinum Exchange Traded Funds with net outflows of 14,750 ounces, mostly due to sales by European investors. Holdings have now retreated below 1.4 million ounces for the first time since February. The year-to-date has, however, seen net buying, albeit at a much lower rate than was the case during 2010. 4 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **19 December 2011** ### **Palladium CFTC data to 13 December 2011; ETF data to 16 December 2011.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Palladium Investment (oz)** |**Date**|**Nymex**

- Palladium’s price was relatively robust throughout mid-December, aided by an investor-driven spike from $640 to $687 from the 6th to the 7th of the month. However, following that move,

worries over the Eurozone weighed as heavily on this metal as on its sister metals. The slide from $685 on the 9th following the latest EU summit to $600 on the 14th perfectly illustrated the market’s view of the outcomes of discussions amongst the various politicians. However, some relatively positive data over car production in the USA and, more generally, globally, provided some strength. More important was the response of investors who drove palladium back to almost $620 later on the 14th. Since that point, a neutral trend in EURUSD has allowed palladium to gain a few Dollars more. While investors would like to be more bullish, macroeconomic trends will dominate their thinking until the end of the year and into January at least. 

- With investor exposure to palladium on the futures exchanges relatively low, there was little further scope for selling in the week to the 13th of December. Net long speculative positions on NYMEX decreased by only a little over 5,000 ounces to 600,000 ounces. With the additional price decline in the past week, we can expect to see further reductions in positioning in the next commitment of traders report. However, the palladium price has remained stronger than might have been expected, suggesting that there is little appetite for increasing short exposure to this metal. 

- For the sixth successive week, palladium ETF holdings declined, falling by 4,300 ounces to 1.78 million ounces on the 16th of December. Although the palladium price has dipped lower during this six week period, it has moved little overall, despite net redemptions of over 110,000 ounces, suggesting that some investors at least remain bullish.
